questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to make money from online videos
Why people share some things online so quickly
The dangers of spending too long on the internet
How cats became popular online
questions.why: Neil says they're talking about why some online content goes viral and some doesn't.

questions.q: What does Neil think of silly online videos?
options: He watches them every day
He only likes videos of animals
He shares them with his friends
He doesn't find them cute or funny
questions.why: Neil says, 'I just don't find silly videos particularly cute – or funny.'

questions.q: According to Dr Jonah Berger, why do we share things?
options: It makes us feel connected and strengthens friendships
It makes us look clever and well informed to others
We want to become famous and get lots of followers
We are bored at work and need something to do
questions.why: He says sharing lets us feel connected and deepen the bonds with our peers and friends.

questions.q: What kind of emotions make us more likely to share, according to Dr Berger?
options: Calm, peaceful emotions that help us relax
Sad emotions, such as feeling lonely or upset
Strong emotions that excite us and make us act
Any emotion at all, as long as it is honest
questions.why: He says high-arousal emotions that 'fire us up and cause us to take action' drive us to share.

questions.q: Which of these does Dr Berger describe as a low-arousal emotion?
options: Anger
Anxiety
Sadness
Humour
questions.why: He lists anger, anxiety, excitement and humour as high arousal; sadness and contentment as low.

questions.q: What surprises Rob about the research?
options: Sad things aren't shared as much as funny things
People share angry content
Older people share more than young people
Cat videos aren't very popular
questions.why: Rob says he's surprised that sad things aren't passed on as much as funny things.

questions.q: Why does Neil ask Rob how often he shares sad videos?
options: Because Neil wants Rob to send him one
To find out if Rob is unhappy
To change the subject
To show that Rob's own habits fit the theory
questions.why: Rob admits 'Good point' and says he tends to share things that make him laugh.

questions.q: What kind of content does Rob mostly share?
options: News that makes him angry
Things that make him laugh
Sad stories
Educational videos
questions.why: Rob says he tends to share content that makes him laugh, like the Grumpy Cat meme.
